r4c.title: New var-expansion test exercises real .mcp.json
r4c.imperative: Confirm McpJsonVarExpansionLaunchTests reads command/args from the committed .mcp.json itself, not a hand-rolled copy.
r4c.finding: Confirmed by reading the test source directly: config = json.loads(MCP_JSON.read_text(...)); entry = config["mcpServers"]["spine"]; proc = subprocess.Popen([entry["command"], *entry["args"]], ..., cwd=str(ROOT)) -- command and args are read live from the committed .mcp.json file on disk, not hand-typed literals; a corruption of .mcp.json (wrong command, wrong args) would break this test. env values (SPINE_FILE/ENGINE/SESSION) are necessarily hand-supplied by the test since .mcp.json stores them as shell dollar-brace-VAR-colon-dash-default template strings and Python has no shell to expand that syntax -- the test docstring is explicit about this substitution and it matches what M1 verified separately (real claude -p dispatch performs the actual dollar-brace expansion). This is not a hand-rolled COPY of command/args (those come from the real file); it is a necessary substitution only for the env values that the file itself cannot supply pre-expanded.
